concepts.description: A quantity that combines enthalpy and entropy to predict whether a process is spontaneous at constant temperature and pressure.
concepts.name: Gibbs Free Energy

concepts.description: Energy is conserved in a system, so energy changes must be accounted for in every process. In this document it is applied to chemical reactions through enthalpy.
concepts.name: First Law of Thermodynamics

concepts.description: A thermodynamic quantity used to track heat exchanged in chemical reactions, applying the first law to reactions at constant pressure.
concepts.name: Enthalpy

concepts.description: The principle introducing entropy and governing the direction in which natural processes proceed.
concepts.name: Second Law of Thermodynamics

concepts.description: A measure of disorder or the number of microstates in a system, used to describe how energy and matter disperse.
concepts.name: Entropy

concepts.description: The tendency of a process to occur without external energy input, predicted here using Gibbs free energy at constant temperature and pressure.
concepts.name: Spontaneity
